message.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>We obtain classical solutions of <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$\lambda $$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mi>λ</mml:mi>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>-deformed <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$\sigma $$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mi>σ</mml:mi>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>-models based on <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$SL(2,{\mathbb {R}})/U(1)$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mrow>
                    <mml:mi>S</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mi>L</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mo>(</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mn>2</mml:mn>
                    <mml:mo>,</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mi>R</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mo>)</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mo>/</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mi>U</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mo>(</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mn>1</mml:mn>
                    <mml:mo>)</mml:mo>
                  </mml:mrow>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> and <jats:italic>SU</jats:italic>(2)/<jats:italic>U</jats:italic>(1) coset manifolds. Using two different sets of coordinates, we derive two distinct classes of solutions. The first class is expressed in terms of hyperbolic and trigonometric functions, whereas the second one in terms of elliptic functions. We analyze their properties along with the boundary conditions and discuss string systems that they describe. It turns out that there is an apparent similarity between the solutions of the second class and the motion of a pendulum.</jats:p>
title: Classical solutions of $$\lambda $$-deformed coset models
